en.name: Flounder
en.summary: Flounder is a lean flatfish with thin, delicate white fillets that cook in minutes and spoil almost as fast. From purchase it keeps 1–2 days in the fridge and 6–8 months in the freezer.
en.pantry: Flounder has no room-temperature life. Flatfish fillets are thin, which means a lot of surface for their weight and very little to buffer them against warmth, and they go slack within an hour or two in a hot kitchen. Bring it home in a cool bag and follow the 2-hour rule, or 1 hour above 32 °C (90 °F). Never leave a tray of fillets on the counter while the oven heats.
en.fridge: Keep flounder at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, on a rack over ice in a container that catches the melt water, and cook it within 1–2 days from purchase. Do not let the fillets sit in liquid — thin flatfish flesh takes up water and turns mushy faster than almost anything else on the slab. A whole flounder keeps slightly better than fillets because the skin and frame protect the flesh, so buy whole if you are not cooking today. Store it on the bottom shelf, below ready-to-eat food.
en.freezer: Flounder keeps 6–8 months at −18 °C (0 °F) — a long window, because lean white flesh has little fat to go rancid. Freeze fillets flat, separated by baking paper, wrapped airtight with no air pockets, or ice-glazed by dipping in cold water. Thin fillets freeze fast and thaw fast, which works in their favour. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; the months are about quality, and flounder dries out and goes cottony at the far end.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge on a plate, which for thin fillets takes only a few hours, or cook them from frozen in a hot pan. Never thaw on the counter, and do not refreeze raw fish.
spoilage: A sour or ammoniacal smell rather than a clean, faintly sweet one.
Flesh that stays dented when pressed instead of springing back.
A milky or sticky film on the fillet, or liquid pooling under it.
Grey or yellowing edges, and flesh that tears when you lift it.
tips: Buy whole if you are not cooking it today; fillets go over faster.
Keep the fillets on a rack, never sitting in melt water.
Freeze thin fillets flat with paper between them, so you can take one at a time.
Cook flounder straight from frozen if you forgot to thaw it — thin fillets cope well.

faq.q: How long does flounder keep in the fridge?
faq.a: 1–2 days from purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, on ice and not sitting in water.
Yes, 6–8 months at −18 °C. Freeze the fillets flat and airtight, or ice-glazed.

faq.q: Can you cook flounder from frozen?
faq.a: Yes. Thin fillets cook well from frozen in a hot pan or oven, and it avoids the mushiness that slow thawing can cause.

faq.q: How can you tell if flounder has gone off?
faq.a: A sour or ammoniacal smell, a milky film on the surface, or flesh that will not spring back when pressed.

zh.name: 比目魚
zh.summary: 比目魚是低脂扁身魚，魚片薄而細嫩，幾分鐘就能煮熟，也幾乎一樣快就會走味。從購買日起冷藏可放 1～2 天，冷凍 6～8 個月。
zh.pantry: 比目魚沒有室溫保存這回事。扁身魚的魚片很薄，相對於重量的表面積很大，幾乎沒有任何緩衝，在熱廚房裡一兩個小時就鬆軟了。請用保冷袋帶回家，並守 2 小時原則，室溫超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時。不要一邊預熱烤箱、一邊把整盤魚片放在檯面上。
zh.fridge: 架在網架上、下面鋪冰，容器要能接住融水，放 4 °C 以下，並在購買後 1～2 天內煮掉。不要讓魚片泡在液體裡——薄的扁魚肉吸水後變糊的速度，大概是魚攤上數一數二快的。整條比魚片耐放一點，因為魚皮和骨架多少保護了魚肉，所以今天不煮就買整條。放最下層，位置低於即食食品。
zh.freezer: 比目魚在 −18 °C 下可放 6～8 個月——這個區間長，是因為低脂白肉幾乎沒有會油耗的脂肪。魚片壓平、中間夾烘焙紙、密封不留空氣，或浸冷水做冰鍍。薄魚片凍得快也解得快，這點反而有利。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，月數講的是品質；放到後段比目魚會乾得像棉絮。
zh.thawing: 放盤子上冷藏解凍，薄魚片只需幾小時；也可以直接從冷凍下熱鍋。不要放室溫解凍，生魚也不要再次冷凍。
spoilage: 聞起來發酸或有氨味，而不是乾淨的淡甜味。
按壓後凹陷回不來，而不是有彈性。
魚片表面出現乳白黏膜，或下方積水。
邊緣泛灰泛黃，拿起來就散。
tips: 今天不煮就買整條；魚片壞得比較快。
架在網架上，不要泡在融水裡。
薄魚片壓平、中間夾紙冷凍，之後一次取一片。
忘了解凍就直接從冷凍下鍋——薄魚片完全可以。

faq.q: 比目魚冷藏可以放多久？
faq.a: 鋪冰、不泡水，放 4 °C 以下，從購買日起 1～2 天。
可以，−18 °C 下 6～8 個月。魚片壓平密封，或做冰鍍。

faq.q: 比目魚可以直接從冷凍下鍋嗎？
faq.a: 可以。薄魚片直接下熱鍋或進烤箱表現很好，還能避免慢慢解凍造成的軟爛。

faq.q: 怎麼判斷比目魚不新鮮了？
faq.a: 發酸或氨味、表面出現乳白黏膜，或按壓後沒有彈性。
